Like they gave her the ring!
They are asking to repeat the ice cream for the room.
They are taking cognac ice cream again!
They definitely want to take all the rings.
I will make one more portion right now.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.trans: Faster!
He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: moving or capable of moving at high speed

examples.trans: We need fast internet.

examples.text: Они сказали, что устанавливают быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: They said that they were installing fast internet.

examples.text: Большое спасибо за вашу быструю помощь!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your quick help!

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

видать.gloss: to see (colloq.: не видать = never to see/get)

meanings.en: не видать (+ dative + genitive) — never to see, never to get
meanings.note: colloquial infinitive and past видал

examples.trans: And you'll never see that flat!
He hasn't been seen for a long time.

examples.text: Скажу, что ты нанял людей меня пытать. И не видать вам квартиры!
examples.trans: I'll say that you hired people to torture me. And you'll never see that flat!

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: See you!
I have a meeting.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'female guest', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: This is a female guest.

examples.text: Все внимание! Гостья пробует блюдо новичка.
examples.trans: Attention everyone! The guest is tasting the newcomer's dish.
The guest is tasting the newcomer's dish.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.trans: Let's talk.
He gives me a book.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Дай! = give (me)!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
Some water, please.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'gesture' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Did you see, she made a gesture!
He wants to fulfill his marital duty!

забрать.gloss: to take back, to take away

meanings.en: to take away, to pick up
meanings.note: забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement
забрать заявление = to withdraw a statement

examples.trans: He will withdraw the statement.
I'll take the keys.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.trans: The town hall called me.
He's from Moscow.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: genitive also 'коньяку' (some cognac)

examples.trans: He drinks French cognac.
The cognac is very expensive.
And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'ice cream' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There the egg white is made of vanilla ice cream.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть мороженое.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always ice cream.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'верный'). Common masculine noun meaning 'infidels / unbelievers' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Come on, infidels, let us hurry along.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть неверный.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always infidels.

meanings.note: one direction, now; 'Неси!' = Bring (it)!

examples.trans: Yulia, bring a pen.
I'm carrying the things.
Yulia, bring a pen and a piece of paper.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'number; phone number; hotel room' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'number; phone number; hotel room' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'number; phone number; hotel room' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Read me the number.
What's your number?
Don't laugh. Read me the number.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Often with annoyance. Core Russian adv meaning 'again' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: It's another trick.
Rain again.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
It's very hard.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'signet / gem ring' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он продал этот перстень и уехал за границу.
examples.trans: He sold that ring and moved abroad.
Can you imagine how much such a ring costs?
I wish I had a ring like that!

повторить.gloss: to repeat, to go over again

meanings.en: to repeat, to say or do again
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'вторить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to repeat, to go over again', paired with 'повторять'.

examples.trans: Right, let's go over it again.
Repeat that, please.
So, repeat that clearly once more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Show me your hands!
Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.en: to please, to be to someone's liking
meanings.note: + dative: тебе понравится = you'll like it

examples.trans: Don't be afraid, you'll like it.
I really liked this film.

examples.text: А придётся! Не бойся, тебе понравится.
examples.trans: Well, you'll have to! Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.en: to try, to have a go
meanings.note: + infinitive. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to try', paired with 'пробовать'.

examples.trans: Let's try.
Try the soup!

examples.text: Как я могу это забыть? Ну, давай попробуем.
examples.trans: How can I forget that? Well, let's try.

meanings.note: International borrowing in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), declined as a regular feminine noun meaning 'portion'.

examples.trans: The waiter brought two portions of salad.

examples.text: И ещё две порции трески с миндалём!
examples.trans: And two more portions of cod with almonds!
Fyodor, prepare two portions of shrimp.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'торапливаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'hurry along'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и поторапливаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and hurry along on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют поторапливаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to hurry along.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (on foot)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.
Bring some water, please.
What did you bring into the flat?

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: I apologise.
He's asking for help.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Thanks, Dad!
Thank you for your trust!

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Give me the keys.
Come here!
The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

тащить.gloss: to drag, to pull, to carry, to bring

meanings.note: colloquial: fetch or drag something

examples.trans: Bring the clothespin quickly!
Then run, go grab a clothespin quickly!

examples.text: Тащи свою птицу су-шефу на стол!
examples.trans: Drag your bird to the sous-chef's table!

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('like') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А она типа не при делах.
examples.trans: And she acts like she had nothing to do with it.

examples.text: Да я не про это. Кто этот тип в коридоре?
examples.trans: That's not what I mean. Who was that guy in the corridor?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Lyolya will definitely come!

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
